analysis:
Examined the MediaIngest.swift inline-video header change (head 769-777, 798-801). Previously only data:video/mp4;base64 and data:video/quicktime;base64 were accepted, compared case-insensitively. Now the header is lowercased and checked for set membership, which adds video/x-m4v and video/mov labels. Both new labels name MP4 or QuickTime containers.

The header is still checked before dataFromDataURI, which applies the decoded-byte cap (maxMediaDecodedBytes). The remaining guards (no file path, memory-backed asset, http/file rejection) are unchanged. Swift's lowercased() and caseInsensitiveCompare differ only in Unicode edge cases. Accepting a non-ASCII lowercase mapping would at worst admit another spelling of the same allowed labels. It does not create a file or URL path.

The new doc comment says MemoryBackedVideoAsset sniffs the container from the bytes. That sniffing is in the mlx-swift-lm submodule, whose bump (7bed821 -> 6aef0a5) has no visible contents. The submodule implements MemoryBackedVideoAsset, UserInput and MediaProcessing, which are T-050 affected files. Its changes to byte sniffing, resource-loader ranges and forbidAll reference restrictions are therefore unverified. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of a regression.

The threat-model edit to T-050 (head 1969-1970) matches the code change. It also claims accepted payloads' bytes are an MP4 or QuickTime file, which depends on the submodule's sniffing. The surrounding threat-model text (T-033..T-058, T-041 detection hint) is unchanged.

No regression is identified for A-001/T-050/TB-003. The next pass should verify that the submodule diff keeps the memory-only asset, container sniffing that rejects non-MP4/QuickTime bytes, and forbidAll reference restrictions.
